answer: Aim for 1.6–2.2 g of protein per kg of bodyweight each day. Spread it across 3–5 meals of 20–40 g each.

knowledge_sources.content:
### Daily Protein Target

Research supports 1.6–2.2 g of protein per kg of bodyweight per day for muscle hypertrophy. Intakes above 2.2 g/kg show diminishing returns.

### Meal Frequency and Dose

Spreading protein across 3–5 meals of 20–40 g each produces more muscle protein synthesis than the same total consumed in fewer large servings.

### Post-Workout Timing

Eating 20–40 g of protein within two hours of training significantly boosts muscle protein synthesis. Leucine-rich sources such as eggs and whey are ideal.

### Protein Sources

Chicken breast, eggs, Greek yogurt, and tuna are high-quality sources rich in all essential amino acids. Well-planned plant diets can meet the same targets.

### Protein While Cutting

During a caloric deficit, targeting 2.0–2.2 g/kg preserves lean muscle and reduces hunger. Higher protein intake also improves dietary adherence.
